videos.script: The people most likely to take a firm's client list out of the building are allowed to read it. {{mistake}} Most of the time nobody means any harm. A spreadsheet mailed home to finish at night. A file uploaded to a converter site. {{doors}} Data loss prevention watches the doors data leaves by. Mail, uploads, sync folders, USB sticks and printers. {{pattern}} In this lesson you write a scanner that finds CPFs and card numbers, and checks their digits the way the issuer does. {{fake}} The data is invented. Nobody real is in it. {{guard}} Then you put the scanner on a folder that syncs to the cloud, and watch it hold back the client list. {{egress}} And you give the workstation a short list of places it may send anything at all. {{law}} Last, the law, and the uncomfortable fact that a DLP tool collects personal data too.
